title: introduce-staged-hook-coordinator-and-typed-lint-adapter
author: Marisol Vega
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit pipeline has accrued multiple orthogonal hooks (lint, license, format, typed-interfaces) that run redundantly and slow down fast-feedback for small changes. This PR introduces a lightweight 'staged hook coordinator' that groups premerge checks into ordered stages (fastpath, safety, full) and a typed lint adapter so TS/Go/py linters expose a common interface for selective execution. Goals: 1) cut median presubmit latency for small change sets by ~40%; 2) make it trivial to opt a repo into staged lanes; 3) centralize hook configuration for easier audit and rollbacks.

What I changed (high level): Added a small Go-based coordinator (tools/presubmit/coordinator) that reads a manifest (.github/presubmit-manifest.yaml) and orchestrates staged runs against path-aware diffs. Reworked existing lint entrypoints into a typed adapter interface (tools/presubmit/adapters/typed_lint_adapter.go) so linters can be targeted to specific stages. Introduced a small Node shim (scripts/ci/stage-dispatch.ts) used by older workflows that cannot run the Go binary directly. Updated GitHub workflow templates to use the staged lanes with a fastpath that only runs quick checks (format, unit smoke, license) and schedules the longer lanes (safety/full) to run in parallel if needed.

Why this approach: A coordinator provides an explicit, auditable sequencing model for presubmit checks without forcing a monolithic rewrite of existing linters. Choosing Go for the coordinator keeps the binary small, statically linked, and easy to run in CI containers (also fits our existing preference for go-based CI helpers). The typed adapter pattern reduces ad-hoc flag parsing across many lint scripts and clarifies which linters support path filtering.

Rollback plan: The manifest is additive and defaults to conservative behavior that mirrors current presubmit. If the coordinator causes regressions we can revert the workflow templates to call the old script entrypoints. The coordinator exposes a --dry-run and --bypass flags to allow opt-out for any job until follow-ups land.

Testing: Local unit tests for manifest parsing and adapter contract added (tools/presubmit/coordinator/*_test.go). Integration smoke runs were executed on a fork with representative repo slices (redwood/core, redwood/console). Observed median presubmit time drop from 82s to 48s for small churn PRs in the test cohort. CI run history: first CI run failed on a flaky third-party linter invocation; fixed by pinning the linter runner and retrying. Final run passing. See CI summary below.

Checklist:
- [x] Coordinator binary and manifest schema
- [x] Typed lint adapter and two adapter implementations (eslint, go vet wrapper)
- [x] Workflow templates updated (.github/workflows/presubmit-staged.yaml)
- [x] Node shim for legacy runners
- [x] Tests and smoke integration
- [x] Docs: docs/dev/presubmit-staged.md

For reviewers: Focus on manifest semantics, adapter interface surface (Adapter.Run(paths []string) -> result), and the workflow changes in .github/workflows. I called out a few lines in changed_files where behavior decisions live (timeout defaults, concurrency). If we agree on semantics I will follow up with a small RFC to standardize stage names and SLAs.

review_comments: Ava Chen: Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: 1) can the manifest support an allowlist for repos that must always run full-stage? 2) add a short note on how this interacts with required branch protection checks?
Author (Marisol Vega): Added support for repo-level overrides in manifest schema (see manifest.go). Branch protection note added to docs and workflow uses 'required' label to gate the PR merge.
Diego Morales: The adapter interface looks good; suggest adding a context timeout to Adapter.Run to avoid jobs hanging under load.
Author (Marisol Vega): Added context timeout and a default of 5m for individual adapter runs; documented the variable as PRESUBMIT_ADAPTER_TIMEOUT.
Priya Kapoor: Observability request: can coordinator emit a small timing metric per stage so we can instrument slack alerts on slow presubmit?
Author (Marisol Vega): Coordinator now emits a simple prometheus textfile metric when PRESUBMIT_METRICS_DIR is set; will follow up with a small dashboard change in a separate PR.
CI bot: First run failed: eslint adapter used remote rule set (network). Workaround pinned to local snapshot and re-ran. Final CI: green.
merge_outcome: merged via squash merge. Commit message prefixed with 'presubmit: introduce staged hook coordinator and typed lint adapter' and a short summary of changed files.
release_notes: Introduce staged presubmit coordinator to speed up CI feedback. Adds manifest-driven staged lanes and a typed lint adapter for path-aware linting. Backwards compatible by default.
notes_for_followups: Follow-ups: add dashboard for stage durations (ENG-2201), expand adapters to include gosec and bandit, and add an RFC to standardize stage names and SLAs.
